\title{benchmark-pelican 0.2.0 package report}
\author{Pooria Arab\\ Independent researcher\\ \texttt{papers@aibenchmarkindex.com}}

\begin{abstract}
Pelican Bicycle SVG (benchmark-pelican) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.2.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 30 tasks at seed 20261015. The review record shows 9 fix rounds, 7 defect classes with public locators, and 5 council-reviewed pull requests of which 4 were approved. Its preregistered trivial-policy best moved from 0.0000 at 0.1.0 to 0.0000 at 0.2.0. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422362, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}

\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-pelican/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
benchmark-pelican is an open-source AI benchmark for SVG drawing and s\allowbreak patial reasoning. It asks models to draw birds riding bicycles, then c\allowbreak hecks the markup and geometry without a model judge.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-pelican/blob/main/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-pelican:README.md\#L7}}.}

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-pelican/docs/grading.md#L3
\begin{quote}
The grader reads SVG text without a browser, renderer, network call, o\allowbreak r model judge. Each task carries its own `metadata.requiredParts` list\allowbreak , so a memorised drawing cannot ace every task. Labels, element IDs, a\allowbreak nd prose do not earn credit.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-pelican/blob/main/docs/grading.md#L3}{\texttt{benchmark-pelican:docs/grading.md\#L3}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Dependency-free structural SVG scan that extracts the single SVG block, applies safety rules, then weights per-part geometry checks from each task's metadata.requiredParts.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-pelican.grader}). \section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records an offline mock run at seed \pkgPublicSeed{} on version \pkgVersion: the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}), the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}), and the seed-1 mock mix scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}). Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.
The README prints a sample run:
% quote: benchmark-pelican/README.md#L34
\begin{quote}

The command prints 30 task rows, a mean score, and a bootstrap 95\% co\allowbreak nfidence interval. A score of 1 means every structural check passed. P\allowbreak artial credit identifies missing geometry in the reason field.

\end{quote}

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set at 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 through a local fake model server answering through the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
The preregistered check ran eight generic trivial policies against this package at versions 0.1.0 and 0.2.0. The best trivial score was \pkgTrivialOld{} at 0.1.0 and \pkgTrivialNew{} at 0.2.0, won by \texttt{\pkgTrivialPolicy{}} (\texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv}).

\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-pelican/README.md#L151
\begin{quote}
The grader checks structure, not visual truth. It verifies that the pa\allowbreak rts each prompt names are present and shaped plausibly; it cannot prov\allowbreak e species, posture, occlusion, or artistic quality. The "does it look \allowbreak like a pelican" question belongs to the optional vision judge, which s\allowbreak tays off by default and unscored. Carefully chosen abstract geometry c\allowbreak an pass.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-pelican/blob/main/README.md#L151}{\texttt{benchmark-pelican:README.md\#L151}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models. The offline numbers are properties of the graders and the scripted policies, not of any hosted model. Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}). Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
